지시사항: Read docs/git-workflow.md for exact Git workflow details.
Use main as the stable demo or release branch.
Use dev as the integration branch.
Create short-lived feature, fix, docs, or chore branches from dev.
Merge normal work back to dev through a PR.
Do not push directly to main or dev.
Do not keep one long-lived personal branch for the whole project.
Use branch format <type>/<domain>-<work>.
Allowed branch types are feature, fix, docs, and chore.
Use lowercase English words and hyphens in branch names.
Do not use Korean, spaces, or personal-name branch schemes.
Start work from the latest dev.
Keep each branch focused on one meaningful task.
Merge latest dev into long-running branches before conflicts grow.
Use commit format <type>: <short summary>.
Allowed commit types are feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, and chore.
Keep each commit focused on one concern.
Open normal work PRs from the work branch into dev.
Keep PRs small; one feature or fix per PR.
Include what changed and why in the PR description.
Get at least one reviewer approval before merge.
Prefer Squash and merge into dev.
Check for conflicts against dev before merge.
Update main only from dev through a PR.
Tag weekly demo versions after merging dev into main.
Remove all conflict markers before committing.
Ask the relevant author before resolving unclear same-file conflicts.
Do not use git push --force.
Do not start member-dependent implementation before the userId contract is finalized.
Do not commit .env, Secret_Key, Supabase keys, tokens, or other secrets.
Do not create huge PRs with unrelated changes.
Do not commit generated dependency or build output such as node_modules, .gradle, build, or bin.
